A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VTC-Bench study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching reformatted results across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-OV-7B, grouped benchmark evaluations, and an inference-time comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds original image-property statistics and qualitative sample analyses in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The procedure remains full-resolution Qwen2-VL filtering, equivalent-ratio downsampling, selection of downsampling failures as Group A, and accuracy aggregation. Newly specifying bicubic interpolation documents implementation without establishing a procedure change.

E1.justification: The eight Qwen2-VL benchmarks and five LLaVA-OV benchmarks remain unchanged, including English and Chinese MMBench. The new analyses reuse existing benchmark groups and represented question types without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 drops Downsample from the main LLaVA-OV-7B comparison at all five compression ratios, although its grouped reference results remain in Appendix Table 6. Other comparator memberships are unchanged; newly cited compression methods are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The original models, pixel bounds, compression ratios, and filtering protocol are retained. Appendix F introduces image-property comparisons on MMStar and POPE at downsampling ratios 2–5, while the isolated latency evaluation in v1 Figure 1b is removed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained accuracy comparisons between groups, Appendix E adds twelve qualitative cases examining detail perception and reasoning. Appendix F adds a quantitative investigation of whether entropy, brightness, contrast, colorfulness, and image dimensions distinguish the groups. These substantially expand validation of the filtering rationale.

E5.justification: Table 7 and Figure 5 newly report means and standard deviations of image properties across samples. Both versions still state that experimental results come from a single run. Appendix F claims no statistically significant differences but identifies no significance test, confidence intervals, or p-values.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark scores in Tables 1–6 are identical. v2 adds image-property results, qualitative examples, and derived comparison annotations; v1's DART/downsampling timings of 0.352/0.125 seconds disappear. One new Table 1 annotation incorrectly shows a 0.9% decrease for VisionZip on POPE at 93.75% reduction, despite its unchanged 80.2 score exceeding downsampling's 79.5.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the operational group definitions are unchanged, and no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added. The new acknowledgment that formal theoretical justification is missing belongs to limitations; the ADR-to-APRR correction clarifies the existing numerical summary.

C1.justification: The task-mismatch finding, downsampling discriminator, and VTC-Bench contributions remain. However, the abstract and introduction now explicitly frame VTC-Bench as an additional assessment or reference benchmark, modestly narrowing its intended role.

C2.justification: Section 6 expands the existing model/filter caveats and adds missing formal justification and restricted method coverage as limitations. Appendices E–F introduce interpretations connecting difficulty to multiple visual details and arguing that low-level image properties cannot explain it, substantially expanding the explanation of the filter's applicability.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies bicubic interpolation, and the front matter adds a project-page link. Hardware, software versions, implementation sources, and compression-control parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its compression-method taxonomy and citations, including VFlowOpt and LUVC, while removing the SEED-Bench citation. New Appendix D substantially develops the distinctions from VisionThink and EffiVLM-Bench, clarifying the paper's benchmarking contribution relative to these already cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and related-work discussion are revised, the exam analogy is removed, and limitations and appendix organization are expanded. ADR is renamed APRR to describe the retained retention scores accurately. The main section sequence and much of the method/results prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 1a and Figure 2 are redrawn and combined into v2 Figure 1; the framework diagram is redesigned, and the latency panel and old results plot disappear. Table 1 adds colored percentage annotations, Tables 2/5/6 combine group entries with gaps, and new Figures 3–5 and Table 7 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 offers a modest net gain through clearer positioning as an additional benchmark, fuller limitations, reproducibility detail, and examples that make the filtering rationale easier to assess. The central benchmark evidence is unchanged, and latency evidence is removed. Appendix F overinterprets overlapping standard deviations without reporting a significance test, while a new percentage annotation is incorrect; these weaknesses limit the improvement.
